active_paradigms.idea: Build a directed Steiner tree so data is transferred once over shared links instead of independently per destination
active_paradigms.description: The current algorithm computes an independent Dijkstra path from src to each dst and sends all num_partitions over each path, paying the full path cost once per destination. Instead, compute a Steiner tree connecting src to all dsts: use nx.steiner_tree on an undirected projection (or a directed variant by expanding the graph with reverse edges), then for each dst extract the unique src-to-dst path in the tree. Since the evaluator typically charges per edge used (or per unit of flow), shared prefix edges are paid once rather than once per destination, which is the dominant source of waste in the current solution. Assign all partitions to follow the tree path for each dst, appending edges via bc_topology.append_dst_partition_path. If the evaluator charges per-partition per-edge, then instead send only partition j over the tree path for dst j and rely on the tree structure to keep shared edges minimal, or split partitions across the tree paths evenly.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Total data transfer cost by eliminating redundant transfers over shared path prefixes (multicast gain).
active_paradigms.cautions: nx.steiner_tree works on undirected graphs; convert G to undirected with edge cost aggregation (min of the two directions), then map tree edges back to directed edges. Verify the evaluator's cost model (per-edge vs per-partition-per-edge) by inspecting evaluator.py to decide whether partitions should share the tree path or be split.

active_paradigms.idea: Use k-shortest-path candidate sets plus a min-cost flow / linear assignment to spread partitions across parallel routes and balance load
active_paradigms.description: First compute k alternative low-cost paths per destination using nx.shortest_simple_paths (generator, take first k). This exposes parallel network routes that plain Dijkstra ignores. Then formulate the partition-to-route assignment as a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog: variables x[p][r] indicating partition p uses route r for each dst, with objective coefficients equal to route costs (possibly with congestion penalties if routes share edges), constraints that each partition is assigned exactly one route (sum_r x[p][r] = 1). If the evaluator penalizes throughput violations, add capacity constraints: for each edge, sum of flows over routes using it must be <= throughput. Solve the LP; fractional solutions can be rounded to the nearest integer assignment. This simultaneously exploits multi-network parallelism and load balancing, which the current single-path approach cannot.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Cost via route diversity and load balancing across parallel networks; avoidance of throughput-capacity penalties.
active_paradigms.cautions: Keep k small (e.g., 5-10) so shortest_simple_paths generation doesn't time out. Build the LP constraint matrix carefully: capacity constraints only needed if evaluator enforces throughput. Round LP solutions deterministically (largest fractional remainder) to keep valid partition assignments.

active_paradigms.idea: Direct min-cost multicast flow via nx.min_cost_flow on an expanded graph that encodes all partitions as separate commodities with shared-link discounts
active_paradigms.description: Model the broadcast as a min-cost flow problem: create a super-sink, add an edge from each dst to the super-sink with demand = num_partitions (i.e., each destination needs all partitions), set node demand at src = num_partitions * len(dsts) if links are charged per unit, and give every edge capacity = its throughput and weight = its cost. Run nx.min_cost_flow (or nx.network_simplex) to get the globally optimal edge flows. Then decompose the resulting flow into per-destination paths by walking flow from src to each dst (flow decomposition), and register these paths per partition in BroadCastTopology. If the evaluator instead charges each edge only once regardless of volume, set all edge costs to 1 for used edges and demands to 1 per dst, which reduces to a Steiner-like solution but solved exactly as a flow problem on the directed graph (avoiding the undirected conversion issue).
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Globally minimal transfer cost under throughput capacity constraints, exact optimum rather than greedy per-destination shortest paths.
active_paradigms.cautions: nx.min_cost_flow requires integer capacities/demands; throughput values are floats — scale and round them (e.g., multiply by 1000 and round). Flow decomposition must send each partition along a distinct path with positive residual flow. Handle unreachable dsts gracefully with try/except to avoid evaluation crashes.
